Treatment

Exosomes

Explore exosome treatments for skin and hair concerns with our medical team.

About the treatment

Exosomes are tiny particles released by cells that carry signals between them. Their use in skin and hair treatments is still being studied, and the evidence varies by product and method.

At your consultation, ask which product would be used, how it is applied and what evidence supports it for your concern. We will discuss expected benefits, uncertainties and other treatment options before you decide.

At a glance

  • Assessment of your skin or hair concern
  • Discussion of the proposed product and method
  • Clear advice on possible side effects and recovery
  • Review of other treatments you are considering
  • A plan to monitor your response

The treatment process

  1. Consultation and assessment. We assess your concern, review your medical history and discuss the evidence for the proposed approach.
  2. A personal plan. We explain the treatment options, likely results, possible side effects and cost before you decide.
  3. The treatment itself. We talk you through the session and check how you feel as we go.
  4. Aftercare and follow up. We explain how to care for the treated area and when to contact us or return for a review.

Expected results

Changes, if any, can take time and vary with the product, method and individual response. We will agree on what to monitor and when to review the result.

Recovery & downtime

Recovery depends on how the product is applied and any procedure used alongside it. If microneedling is involved, temporary redness and sensitivity may occur. We will give you instructions for cleansing, sun protection and when to resume your usual products.

Who is it for?

A consultation is needed for skin texture or hair thinning concerns. We first assess the likely cause, then discuss whether the proposed treatment is appropriate and what alternatives are available.

Frequently asked questions

What exactly are exosomes?
Exosomes are tiny particles that help cells communicate. Products used in aesthetic treatments can differ in their source and contents, so ask about the specific product and evidence for its use.
Is it the same as PRP?
No. PRP is prepared from a sample of your own blood. Exosome products are different preparations, and their contents and evidence vary. We can explain both approaches at your consultation.
When do results appear?
There is no reliable timeline that applies to everyone. We will explain what is known about the proposed product and set a review date to assess your response.
